To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and evaluated a novel method to assign new change requests to developers based on their previous change requests, and that the proposed method is able to suggest developers that have solved change requests similar to the new one with a precision of 0.7.

(a) the textual description of open source change requests is useful to index developers as information retrieval documents, (b) the textual description and the history of change requests is useful for suggesting the best candidate developers to solve a new change request.

1) change requests in software repositories are a good source of information for suggesting the best candidate developers to handle a change request; 2) a simple information retrieval method can be used for this purpose; 3) the method can be improved by using a relevance feedback approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to automatically suggest the best candidate developers to handle a change request?
the study of the assignment of developers to change requests and with the proposal of a method to suggest developers to resolve a change request based on a similarity analysis of change requests.
the problem of supporting the assignment of change requests in software repositories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods introduced in the paper have been able to identify developers with high precision, but low recall, for both the projects considered.
the proposed method is a promising and effective way of suggesting the most appropriate developer to resolve a given change request.
the method is effective in assigning change requests to developers, especially in projects where developers work on a wide variety of change request types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods are able to provide good results, but that they are not yet able to be fully automatic.
the method is effective and the results are promising.
our methods can be successfully applied to the analysis of open source software repositories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis and the method introduced in this paper are useful to identify the set of best candidates to resolve a new request and to evaluate their competencies.
it is possible to use the textual description in change request repositories to identify the developers most suitable for a new change request assignment.

it is possible to identify the best candidates to assign a new change request to, based only on the textual description of the change request and on the textual description and the assignment of previous change requests.
